answer: Under combinatorial kinship tolls, every new identity on the oasis network submits a unique pair of a physical coupon and a latency-fingerprint path; if a hash collides with any prior identity at three or more matched components, the attacker must re-acquire fresh coupons for all their kin, since each identity near a claimed vertex or inlet counts as related. Coupons are ferrous-inked paper tokens mailed once per address, so minting ten fakes costs ten shipments and ten distinct routes, while an honest agent pays only one shipment and one route, keeping entry cheap.
